title: Security triage & audit-schema cheat sheet
body:
Purpose: Quick-reference triage runbook and audit-log schema mapping for on-call security responders. This is a compact cheat-sheet intended for live incidents to: speed evidence capture, normalize audit fields for SIEM exports, and remind responders of RBAC/chain-of-custody rules.

Scope: Applies to hosted, dedicated, and private deployments (control plane and edge infra). Not a replacement for the full forensics playbook — use this to stabilize and preserve evidence within the first 60 minutes.

Summary (1-line): Identify impact, take containment steps that preserve logs, export normalized audit slices to SIEM, and initiate chain-of-custody.

Initial triage checklist (first 15 min):
- Acknowledge and record the alert: incident_id = sec-YYYYMMDD-<oncall>-<counter>.
- Classify scope: control-plane | customer-vpc | runtime-gpu | api-ingress.
- ETA for hands-on: oncall starts within 5 min, escalate to SecOps lead if >= 15 min delay.
- Snapshot volatile state (do not reboot): capture process list, network connections, open sockets, kernel messages. Use commands below.
- Set evidence preservation flag in ticketing system and tag relevant alerts in SIEM.

Severity guide (fast):
- Sev 1: active data exfiltration, credential compromise with lateral movement, or customer-impacting outage.
- Sev 2: suspicious privileged actions, unusual API key activity, or evidence of attempted exploit.
- Sev 3: low-risk anomalies (failed logins, single non-critical config change).

Commands & capture snippets (examples):
- Process snapshot (control plane hosts): ps auxww > /tmp/sec-procs-$(date +%s).txt
- Netstat + conntrack: ss -tulpen > /tmp/sec-ss-$(date +%s).txt; sudo conntrack -L > /tmp/sec-conn-$(date +%s).txt
- Kernel logs (last 4k lines): journalctl -k -n 4000 > /tmp/sec-kern-$(date +%s).log
- Container runtime: crictl ps -a --output json > /tmp/sec-cri-$(date +%s).json
- Kubernetes: kubectl get pods -A -o wide --show-labels > /tmp/sec-k8s-pods-$(date +%s).txt
- Active API sessions (auth service): curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' https://auth.internal/api/sessions | jq . > /tmp/sec-sessions-$(date +%s).json
- Hash evidence artifacts (SHA256): sha256sum /tmp/<file> > /tmp/<file>.sha256

Audit log schema (canonical fields to extract and why):
- timestamp: ISO8601 UTC (event ordering). Example: 2026-01-12T15:14:03Z
- event_id: unique uuid (correlates across systems).
- actor_id: internal user id or service principal (map to RBAC).
- actor_type: human | service | api_key | pipeline
- role: pre-change role label (RBAC v2 role.name)
- action: human-readable verb (e.g., auth.login, model.deploy, cache.clear)
- resource_type: e.g., project, model, deployment, secret, vm
- resource_id: canonical resource identifier (project:proj-123, model:model-llama-70b-v2)
- src_ip: source IP (attestation for geo/ASN checks)
- user_agent: client/SDK info 
- request_id: tracing id connecting API and infra logs
- outcome: success | failure | throttled | partial
- reason: free-text or structured code (e.g., RATE_LIMITED, INVALID_TOKEN)
- raw_payload_ref: storage path/retention pointer for full payload (s3://sec-archives/2026/01/12/...)
- retention_tier: hot | warm | cold (guides SIEM export windows)

Why this mapping: Consistent keys let automated parsers enrich and normalize events before SIEM ingestion (reduces false positives, enables automated rollback triggers for specific actions).

Example normalized audit event (single-line JSON for SIEM):
{"timestamp":"2026-01-12T15:14:03Z","event_id":"8a9f2b4e-...","actor_id":"user:leah.moreno","actor_type":"human","role":"sec:incident-responder","action":"deployment.delete","resource_type":"deployment","resource_id":"deploy-7a3f","src_ip":"34.82.112.10","user_agent":"redwood-cli/1.6.0","request_id":"trace-abc123","outcome":"success","reason":"manual-delete","raw_payload_ref":"s3://sec-archives/2026/01/12/trace-abc123.json","retention_tier":"hot"}

SIEM export checklist (Splunk / Elastic / Chronicle patterns):
- Determine time window (t0-30m to t0+30m as default), then expand if evidence indicates wider blast radius.
- Query patterns to run immediately (examples):
  - API key anomalies: index=audit (action:sdk.request OR actor_type:api_key) | stats count by actor_id, src_ip | where count>50
  - Privilege changes: index=audit action:role.update OR action:role.bind | table timestamp, actor_id, role, resource_id, request_id
  - Large data transfer: index=network bytes>10000000 | sort -bytes
- Export format: newline-delimited JSON with the canonical fields above. Include raw_payload_ref for payload retrieval.
- Export destination: sec-siem-staging/<incident_id>/normalized.jsonl (S3) and notify SIEM ingestion team via ticket.

Automation and alerts: what to turn on quickly
- Ingest normalized audit events and map actor_id to user directory (LDAP/Okta) before enrichment.
- High-confidence automated actions (only with RBAC-safe allowlist): auto-suspend compromised API keys, remove ephemeral credentials, but do NOT auto-revoke infra-admin roles without human review.
- Use enrichment hooks: geoip, ASN, login_time_baseline, and recent_role_changes.

RBAC v2 considerations for emergency escalation:
- Use the emergency_role: sec-oncall-esc with limited elevated privileges (timeboxed, logged).
- All emergency_role grants must be annotated in the ticket with grant_id and TTL.
- Prefer short-lived service tokens over permanent role edits. Record actor, grant_id, TTL, and approval channel in the evidence bundle.
footer_notes:
Chain-of-custody: ensure all artifacts have hashes and are uploaded to the incident archive before moving or rebooting hosts. Retention guidance: 'hot' tier = 90 days, 'warm' = 1 year, 'cold' = 7 years (compliance exception required for >7 years).

Communication templates (Slack snippets):
- Initial alert to #sec-oncall: [INCIDENT sec-2026-0012] Sev2 - suspected API key misuse. Oncall: @leah_moreno. Triage running. Do not escalate externally until confirmed.
- External customer notification (short): We are investigating authentication anomalies affecting API tokens. No customer data exposure confirmed. We'll provide updates at T+60m.

Post-incident postmortem brief template (quick fields to fill):
- Incident id, dates/times (detect, respond, remediate, close).
- Severity and impacted systems.
- Root cause (one-liner).
- Evidence preserved (paths + hashes).
- Timeline (bullet events with timestamps).
- Mitigation actions and owner + ETA.
- Follow-ups (policy, infra, telemetry changes).

Contacts (Escalation matrix):
- Oncall Security: sec-oncall@redwood.ai (rotating pager)
- SecOps Lead: Omar Patel (omar@redwood.ai)
- Infra Pager: infra-oncall@redwood.ai
- Legal (privacy): legal-privacy@redwood.ai

Notes and gotchas:
- When exporting logs from private deployments, follow customer-approved evidence export agreements — do not transfer PII off-customer premises unless contract allows.
- Normalizing timestamps is critical: prefer service-level tracers' request_id to join events across systems.
- If the incident touches KMS keys or HSM access, pause automated retention and engage crypto team immediately.

Revision history: Drafted by Leah Moreno 2025-11-08; major cleanup with audit schema added 2026-01-14; added SIEM export patterns 2026-02-20.
